newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Arab League says Algeria's campaign mirrors democracy.
newsitem.headline: Arab League says Algeria's campaign mirrors democracy.

text.p: Arab League deputy chief Said Kamel, heading a 61-strong team to supervise Algeria's June 5 parliamentary election, on Sunday hailed the poll campaign as an example for free speech and political opinion for other Arab countries.
"The election campaigning confirmed the fair democratic experience in Algeria and showed a free speech and freedom of opinion in the country," he told a news conference.
Kamel said the league's observers would be dispatched over Algeria's 48 provinces to watch the polling in order to prepare a report on the fairness of voting.

"The poll campaigning mirrors a fair multi-party democratic experience in Algeria...The election is a good starting point for other elections...enriching our experiences (in other Arab countries)," he said.
More than 200 officials from the Arab League, the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) and the United Nations have arrived in Algeria at the invitation of the government to monitor the poll.

Campaigning ends on Monday for a 48-hour cooling-off period for voters to reflect on their choices among nearly 8,000 candidates from 39 parties and independent contenders ahead of the ballot on Thursday.
Algeria has been without an elected parliament since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.

Western diplomats estimate about 60,000 people have died in the violence which rapidly erupted and which has continued for more than five years. The secular opposition Socialist Forces Front party last week put the death toll at about 120,000 people.
